newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom gets 25 pct of transponder firm.
newsitem.headline: Telkom gets 25 pct of transponder firm.

text.p: Indonesian transponder operator PT Citra Sari Makmur said on Friday it had given telecommunications giant PT Telkom a 25 percent stake in the company to ensure long-term business prospects.

Citra Sari Makmur is a joint venture with Bell Atlantic Indonesia, Inc. holding a 36.71 percent stake and Indonesian businessman Subagio Wirjoatmodjo, who is the company's president-director 38.29 percent.
Subagio said in a statement the existing shareholders decided to give the other 25 percent stake to Telkom for long-term strategic business reasons.
The statement said the 25 percent stake is valued at 5.3 billion rupiah.
Previously, PT Telkom and PT Citra Sari Makmur had cooperated since 1989 under a joint operation scheme, through which Telkom received 10 percent of the revenue.
A Telkom spokesman said PT Citra Sari Makmur reported net profit of 9.77 billion rupiah in 1995.
PT Citra Sari Makmur rents a satellite transponder from Telkom and leases lines for corporate communications.
